The horror home screen for Android TV

SCARY Scan to donate

The home screen that makes you leave the lights on.

SCARY turns your Android TV into a horror cinema. 170 hand-picked horror films and thrillers and 40 series with real posters, a new film for tonight every evening, rows from the web that never run out, and Stremio, Google Play and all your apps in one place.

Download scary.apk Support SCARY
  • Free
  • 2.9 MB
  • Android TV 8.0 and up
  • No account, no ads

What you get

A cinema of fear, on the remote you already have

  • 170 films and 40 series New

    Hand-picked horror and psychological thrillers, each with a fear meter from 1 to 5. A Series tab brings Hill House, Stranger Things, Dark, Kingdom and more.

  • Rows that never run out

    Popular now, new this year, sci-fi horror, crime and suspense, and year after year back to 1920: rows from the web keep loading for as long as you scroll.

  • Your phone is the remote New

    Scan the code on the TV and your phone's browser takes over: arrows, search, and pasting a TMDB key in a second. Turn on SCARY's accessibility service and it controls Stremio and other apps too. Home Wi-Fi only, every command signed and encrypted, nothing to install.

  • Bucket list New

    Pick a few films, press Start, and they play one after another: each time you come back from Stremio, SCARY offers the next one.

  • What do you feel like tonight?

    Eight moods, from mind games and "short and sharp" to "slow-burn dread", or pick a decade. Plus rows for found footage, folk and Asian horror, zombies, vampires and haunted houses.

  • How much time do you have? New

    Up to 90 minutes, an evening, a double feature or a marathon: SCARY lines up the films and numbers them in the order to watch.

  • The shiver

    The film's title trembles and flickers in the dark for a moment before the movie opens.

  • Where to watch

    Look the film up in the apps you have, such as Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, YouTube and Plex, or in Google TV search. Not there? With a TMDB key, it shows where to rent or buy it in your country. A QR code on every film page opens it on your phone, ready to share.

  • Family night

    Only the gentlest films, everywhere in the app. Leaving family night takes your PIN.

  • My list, Watched and Loved it

    Hold OK on a poster to keep it. SCARY marks a film as watched when you come back from it, "Loved it" brings more like it, "Not for me" keeps it out of suggestions, and "Your year in fear" sums it all up.

  • Search, or be surprised

    By text or voice, in the library and across the web (horror, thriller and mystery only). Or "Surprise me": a random film at the fear level you pick, preferring ones you haven't seen.

  • Five languages

    English, Hebrew, Arabic, Portuguese and Russian, right to left where it should be. Full TalkBack and remote support.

Install in three minutes

From download to your new home screen

  1. Allow the install

    On the TV, open Settings → Device Preferences → Security & restrictions and allow installs from unknown sources for the app you will install with.

  2. Get scary.apk onto the TV

    Download it on the TV with a downloader app, or on your phone and send it with an app like Send Files to TV. Developers can use adb install scary.apk.

  3. Make SCARY the home screen

    Open SCARY and choose Make SCARY the home screen. If your TV offers no choice, turn on SCARY Home button in the accessibility settings.

Tip: once SCARY is on the TV, open Settings → Phone remote and scan the code. Your phone becomes the remote, and pasting a TMDB key takes a second.

Download link

Always the latest build, tested on a TV emulator before it is published. A new build installs over the old one and keeps your settings.

Download scary.apk Release notes

Not on Google Play yet: this is a personal-use build you install yourself.

No video, no illegal files

SCARY does not host, store, stream, search for or link to video files, legal or otherwise. It shows public movie information such as titles, posters and ratings, and opens the movie in a streaming app that is already installed on the same device: your TV, or a tablet or phone if you install SCARY there. Playback happens entirely in that app, under its terms. SCARY installs and recommends no add-ons.

No account, no ads, no tracking. Your list, settings and PIN stay on your TV.

Privacy, cookies and accessibility

The fine print, in plain words

Draft, pending legal reviewVersion 1.1 · Last updated 31 October 2026

Privacy policy

Who is responsible

This page and the SCARY app are an open-source project by diamondrubinny. To reach us about privacy, email d@rubinny.net. For general questions you can also open an issue at github.com/diamondrubinny/Scary/issues, but please don't post personal details in a public issue.

What this page collects

Nothing. There are no forms, no accounts, no analytics and no advertising, and the page loads no outside fonts or scripts.

What stays in your browser

  • Your cookie choice and the date you made it, so the page doesn't ask again. This is strictly necessary to respect your choice.
  • The language you picked, only if you allow Preferences.

Both are kept in your browser's local storage on your device. We never receive them. Change your choice in Privacy and cookie settings, or delete them by clearing this site's data in your browser.

Hosting

Like every website, the service that delivers this page receives technical data such as your IP address and browser type, to deliver it and keep it secure. That processing follows the hosting service's own privacy policy.

Download and donations

The download button opens GitHub and the donate button opens PayPal. Those sites process your data under their own privacy policies. Donations are handled entirely by PayPal. PayPal may share details such as your name, email address and the amount with the recipient, as described in PayPal's terms.

The app

The SCARY app has its own privacy notice: docs/PRIVACY.md. In short: no account, no ads and no tracking; your settings stay on your TV.

Legal basis and your rights

Remembering your language is based on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time. Storing your cookie choice is needed to comply with the law. Under the Israeli Privacy Protection Law and, where it applies, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you can ask to see, correct or delete personal data about you, object to its use, and complain to the Privacy Protection Authority in Israel or to the data protection authority in your EU country. Because this page collects no personal data, we usually hold nothing about you.

Cookie policy

This page sets no cookies of its own. It keeps the two items below in your browser's local storage, which privacy law treats the same way as cookies. There are no analytics, advertising or social media trackers.

NameWhat it keepsCategoryHow longShared with others
scary.consentYour cookie choice, the policy version and the dateEssential, always onUntil you change it or clear site dataNo
scary.langThe language you pickedPreferences, only with your consentUntil you withdraw consent or clear site dataNo

Analytics: none. Marketing: none. If this policy changes, the page asks for your choice again. If you view this page through a service that sets its own cookies (for example to keep you signed in), those are covered by that service's cookie policy.

Accessibility statement

We want everyone to be able to read this page and install SCARY, including people who use a screen reader, a keyboard or a magnifier. The page aims to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA and the Israeli Standard IS 5568.

What we did

  • Semantic headings and landmarks, and a "Skip to content" link.
  • Everything works with a keyboard, with a clearly visible focus ring.
  • Text descriptions for every image, including the screenshots.
  • Right-to-left layout for Hebrew and Arabic, and the page language set for screen readers.
  • Strong colour contrast, text that can be zoomed to 200% and a layout that fits phones.
  • No flashing. The logo dims twice when the page loads, and not at all if your device asks for reduced motion.

Known limitations

  • The screenshots show the app in English; their text descriptions are translated.
  • The page has been checked by its developers but not yet audited by an accessibility expert.

Report a problem

If something is hard to use, email d@rubinny.net or open an issue at github.com/diamondrubinny/Scary/issues. Describe the page, the problem and the device or assistive technology you use. We aim to reply within 14 days.
